26: /** A {@link BreakIterator} that splits sentences using an OpenNLP sentence chunking model. */
27: public final class OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator extends BreakIterator {
28: 
29:   private CharacterIterator text;
30:   private int currentSentence;
31:   private int[] sentenceStarts;
32:   private NLPSentenceDetectorOp sentenceOp;
33: 
34:   public OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator(NLPSentenceDetectorOp sentenceOp) {
35:     this.sentenceOp = sentenceOp;
36:   }
37: 
38:   @Override
39:   public int current() {
40:     return text.getIndex();
41:   }
42: 
43:   @Override
44:   public int first() {
45:     currentSentence = 0;
46:     text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
47:     return current();
48:   }
49: 
50:   @Override
51:   public int last() {
52:     if (sentenceStarts.length > 0) {
53:       currentSentence = sentenceStarts.length - 1;
54:       text.setIndex(text.getEndIndex());
55:     } else { // there are no sentences; both the first and last positions are the begin index
56:       currentSentence = 0;
57:       text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
58:     }
59:     return current();
60:   }
61: 
62:   @Override
63:   public int next() {
64:     if (text.getIndex() == text.getEndIndex() || 0 == sentenceStarts.length) {
65:       return DONE;
66:     } else if (currentSentence < sentenceStarts.length - 1) {
67:       text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[++currentSentence]);
68:       return current();
69:     } else {
70:       return last();
71:     }
72:   }
73: 
74:   @Override
75:   public int following(int pos) {
76:     if (pos < text.getBeginIndex() || pos > text.getEndIndex()) {
77:       throw new IllegalArgumentException("offset out of bounds");
78:     } else if (0 == sentenceStarts.length) {
79:       text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
80:       return DONE;
81:     } else if (pos >= sentenceStarts[sentenceStarts.length - 1]) {
82:       // this conflicts with the javadocs, but matches actual behavior (Oracle has a bug in
83:       // something)
84:       // https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8015110
85:       text.setIndex(text.getEndIndex());
86:       currentSentence = sentenceStarts.length - 1;
87:       return DONE;
88:     } else { // there are at least two sentences
89:       currentSentence = (sentenceStarts.length - 1) / 2; // start search from the middle
90:       moveToSentenceAt(pos, 0, sentenceStarts.length - 2);
91:       text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[++currentSentence]);
92:       return current();
93:     }
94:   }
95: 
96:   /** Binary search over sentences */
97:   private void moveToSentenceAt(int pos, int minSentence, int maxSentence) {
98:     if (minSentence != maxSentence) {
99:       if (pos < sentenceStarts[currentSentence]) {
100:         int newMaxSentence = currentSentence - 1;
101:         currentSentence = minSentence + (currentSentence - minSentence) / 2;
102:         moveToSentenceAt(pos, minSentence, newMaxSentence);
103:       } else if (pos >= sentenceStarts[currentSentence + 1]) {
104:         int newMinSentence = currentSentence + 1;
105:         currentSentence = maxSentence - (maxSentence - currentSentence) / 2;
106:         moveToSentenceAt(pos, newMinSentence, maxSentence);
107:       }
108:     } else {
109:       assert currentSentence == minSentence;
110:       assert pos >= sentenceStarts[currentSentence];
111:       assert (currentSentence == sentenceStarts.length - 1 && pos <= text.getEndIndex())
112:           || pos < sentenceStarts[currentSentence + 1];
113:     }
114:     // we have arrived - nothing to do
115:   }
116: 
117:   @Override
118:   public int previous() {
119:     if (text.getIndex() == text.getBeginIndex()) {
120:       return DONE;
121:     } else {
122:       if (0 == sentenceStarts.length) {
123:         text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
124:         return DONE;
125:       }
126:       if (text.getIndex() == text.getEndIndex()) {
127:         text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
128:       } else {
129:         text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[--currentSentence]);
130:       }
131:       return current();
132:     }
133:   }
134: 
135:   @Override
136:   public int preceding(int pos) {
137:     if (pos < text.getBeginIndex() || pos > text.getEndIndex()) {
138:       throw new IllegalArgumentException("offset out of bounds");
139:     } else if (0 == sentenceStarts.length) {

141:       currentSentence = 0;
142:       return DONE;
143:     } else if (pos < sentenceStarts[0]) {
144:       // this conflicts with the javadocs, but matches actual behavior (Oracle has a bug in

152:       moveToSentenceAt(pos, 0, sentenceStarts.length - 1);
153:       if (0 == currentSentence) {
154:         text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
155:         return DONE;
156:       } else {
157:         text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[--currentSentence]);
158:         return current();
159:       }
160:     }
161:   }
162: 
163:   @Override
164:   public int next(int n) {
165:     currentSentence += n;
166:     if (n < 0) {
167:       if (text.getIndex() == text.getEndIndex()) {
168:         ++currentSentence;
169:       }
170:       if (currentSentence < 0) {
171:         currentSentence = 0;
172:         text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
173:         return DONE;
174:       } else {

176:       }

178:       if (currentSentence >= sentenceStarts.length) {

180:         text.setIndex(text.getEndIndex());
181:         return DONE;
182:       } else {
183:         text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
184:       }
185:     }
186:     return current();
187:   }

192:   }

195:   public void setText(CharacterIterator newText) {
196:     text = newText;
197:     text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
198:     currentSentence = 0;
199:     Span[] spans = sentenceOp.splitSentences(characterIteratorToString());
200:     sentenceStarts = new int[spans.length];
201:     for (int i = 0; i < spans.length; ++i) {
202:       // Adjust start positions to match those of the passed-in CharacterIterator
203:       sentenceStarts[i] = spans[i].getStart() + text.getBeginIndex();
204:     }
205:   }

207:   private String characterIteratorToString() {
208:     String fullText;
209:     if (text instanceof CharArrayIterator) {
210:       CharArrayIterator charArrayIterator = (CharArrayIterator) text;
211:       fullText =
212:           new String(
213:               charArrayIterator.getText(),
214:               charArrayIterator.getStart(),
215:               charArrayIterator.getLength());
216:     } else {
217:       // TODO: is there a better way to extract full text from arbitrary CharacterIterators?
218:       StringBuilder builder = new StringBuilder();
219:       for (char ch = text.first(); ch != CharacterIterator.DONE; ch = text.next()) {
220:         builder.append(ch);
221:       }
222:       fullText = builder.toString();
223:       text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
224:     }
225:     return fullText;
226:   }

Fixed. In `preceding()` (lucene/analysis/opennlp/src/java/org/apache/lucene/analysis/opennlp/OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator.java:151), changed the middle-search start from `sentenceStarts.length / 2` to `(sentenceStarts.length - 1) / 2`, matching `following()`, which prevents `moveToSentenceAt` from indexing out of bounds when there are only 2 sentences.

All 9 tests in `TestOpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator` (including `testPrecedingWithTwoSentences`) pass.
